hero.headline: It knows when to start over
hero.sub: A long conversation used to get quietly more expensive until it broke. ECO mode gives the window a plan: at the token count you set, the agent writes its own state into the task and carries on in a fresh session — and the window itself stops being a percentage you have to interpret.

shot.alt: The context popover: 'Context window 45%', a bar drawn as three bands — the first filled, the second a third amber, the third untouched — then '450k / 1.0M' and '550k free', and a lit ECO pill reading 'hands off at 200k'.
shot.caption: The pill IS the control. Lit, it names the count it hands off at.

items.title: 45% told you nothing
items.text: One bar and one number cannot say which KIND of full you are. The window is now three bands — up to 350k, up to 650k, and the rest — so the count of lit bands is legible at a glance in a way a percentage never was.

items.title: A small window draws one
items.text: The edges are clamped to the real limit, so a 200k-window model collapses to a single band instead of drawing two dead rings it can never reach.

items.title: ECO is a handover, not a trim
items.text: At the mark, the agent writes what it is doing into the task — done, next, decisions, what it learned — and a fresh session picks the task up from there. Nothing is summarised away behind your back.

items.title: It is per chat, and it is a pill
items.text: One click under the bar it changes. Off is off: the conversation runs to the end of the window the way it always did.

blocks.title: J.A.R.V.I.S — and it says ALPHA
blocks.body: Talk to the agent and it talks back: hold the microphone, or Alt+Space from anywhere in the app, and the answer comes back in two or three plain sentences. It works end to end, and it is earlier than beta — so the card says so rather than sitting there unlabelled and reading as finished.

shot.alt: The composer's mode menu: four cards — Basic, Plan, Develop, and J.A.R.V.I.S, which is selected and carries an ALPHA chip beside its name.
shot.caption: One word, on every surface that announces the mode.

blocks.title: Hold a key and speak
blocks.body: The mode tells you how to use it without being asked. Let go and the take is sent; the structure that would have been read aloud arrives on screen instead.

shot.alt: The chat composer in J.A.R.V.I.S mode: a mode chip reading J.A.R.V.I.S, a microphone button, and the instruction 'Hold Alt+Space or the mic to speak'.
shot.caption: Push-to-talk, in the composer you were already looking at.

blocks.title: One key, and the parts worth tuning
blocks.body: Everything runs through OpenRouter on a single key, stored on this machine at 0600 and never in a project, so a team sync cannot carry it anywhere. The card can say a key is set and can never show it to you, because no route returns it. A whisper model installed here transcribes locally; with none, the take goes to the API — and the setting says which.

shot.alt: The Voice card in Settings → Agents, badged ALPHA: an OpenRouter key field reading 'No key', an optional Groq key, a push-to-talk key set to Alt+Space, 'Hold to speak', a voice picker, a transcriber set to 'Automatic — local if installed', automatic speech-language detection, a 'Speak answers' switch and a speaking-speed picker.
shot.caption: Folded at the bottom of Agents until you want it.

blocks.title: The shape is drawn, not read out
blocks.body: Behind the agent's HTML there is now a real layout engine. The answer names the boxes and which ones connect; the kit places them and draws the arrows, including the ones that branch and rejoin. Nothing here is positioned by hand, and a chain that fits on one line stays a sentence.

shot.alt: An agent-drawn diagram of a card payment: Payment submitted leads to an Authorised? decision, which branches to a green Order placed on yes and to a Retryable code? decision on no, which branches to a red Declined for good and to Second attempt — and Second attempt loops back into Authorised?.
shot.caption: The loop back into 'Authorised?' is the part a list of steps cannot show.

blocks.title: A percent is not a percent
blocks.body: Every account bar now says how much of its window is LEFT, not what time it resets — because 88% with fifty minutes to run and 73% with two days to run are nothing alike, and a clock makes you do that arithmetic yourself. The same fact reached the chooser: usage enters the score multiplied by the share of its window still ahead, so a window about to be forgiven stops being treated as spent.

shot.alt: Three connected Claude accounts, each with a 5-hour bar and a weekly bar: 34% with 3h 9m left and 61% with 3d 23h left; 7% with 4h 37m left and 22% with 5d 23h left; and, in amber, 88% with 48m left and 73% with 1d 23h left.
shot.caption: 88% with fifty minutes left is a different account from 73% with two days.

blocks.title: Your accounts, your policy
blocks.body: Auto-switch used to have one opinion compiled into it. Now you choose what a second account is FOR: spread the load so every account stays healthy, or drain the list in order so one window is spent to the last turn before the next is touched.

shot.alt: The auto-switch policy in Settings → Agents: 'Spread the load (weighted score)' selected over 'Drain in order', and three weight fields — 5-hour window 1, weekly window 2, place in the list 5 — above the formula 'score = 1·5-hour% + 2·weekly% + 5·place in list — the lowest score serves the next turn.'
shot.caption: The formula is printed under the fields, so a surprising switch is explicable.

blocks.text: J.A.R.V.I.S is ALPHA and desktop-only — the web dashboard has no microphone path, so a button there would be a control that cannot work. Without a key the mode still runs as text; it just cannot listen or speak.

closer.title: Where to start
closer.body: Open the context reading in the composer and light the ECO pill. Voice lives in Settings → Agents → Voice, then pick J.A.R.V.I.S from the mode menu.
